provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite provider; accounting SaaS provider
implementation_statement: Each SaaS provides the account functions. The owner has one named account in each service, and the bookkeeper has its own accountant-role account in the accounting SaaS. Gap: accounts are never reviewed; the router maker's cloud portal account used for Customer B's equipment is the owner's own login; accounts on the old laptop were never removed.
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-016, G-018)

implementation_statement: The owner uses one administrator account on the laptop for email, web, and engineering work. By 2026-10-31 the owner creates a standard daily account and keeps a separate administrator account only for installing software; engineering software runs under the standard account wherever its maker allows.
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-018)

implementation_statement: Remote work for Customer A goes only through Customer A's gateway (named account, MFA, per-session approval, recorded by Customer A). Gap: the owner's cellular router at Customer B was always on, reached through a password-only cloud portal, with no per-session approval and no written approval from plant management; its local admin page accepted the factory default password (P07, 2026-08-27; changed that day). Since 2026-09-03 the router is powered off except for sessions Customer B approves by phone. It is to be replaced by a Customer B owned gateway or removed by 2026-12-31.
evidence: Router portal settings; P07 test at Customer B 2026-08-27; Customer B decision 2026-09-03
regulatory_driver: Customer A exhibit S2 (P03 G-037); CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-017, G-018, G-027)

implementation_statement: The phone has a passcode, device encryption, and remote wipe; work email is in the suite's app. Gap: photos of customer wiring and HMI screens stay in the camera roll, which syncs to the owner's personal photo cloud. From 2026-10-31 equipment photos go to the job folder in the business file plan and are deleted from the camera roll.
regulatory_driver: Customer A exhibit S1 (P03 G-036); Customer B and C NDAs (P03 G-044)

implementation_statement: The laptop connects to customer machine networks only at the customer's request and only to the machine the job needs. Gap: there is no written rule for what the laptop may do on a customer network, and at Customer A the media scanning station was skipped on about 6 night breakdown calls in 12 months. POL-01 section 7 sets the rule from 2026-09-11.
evidence: Owner self-review; Customer A scanning station log (requested)
regulatory_driver: Customer A exhibit S3 (P03 G-038); CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-024, G-027)

implementation_statement: The owner has had no security training. By 2026-12-31 the owner completes a general security awareness course and a free online industrial control system security course from a government training portal, then repeats awareness training every year.
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-020)

implementation_statement: An equipment list exists for insurance (laptop, phone, instruments). Gap: no list of engineering software and licenses, USB sticks, the router at Customer B, or the SaaS services, and no index of the Customer Machine Library showing the current version of each program. The asset list is POL-01 Appendix A; the library index is due 2026-10-31.
evidence: Insurance equipment list; library folder review 2026-08-25
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-007, G-008, G-009, G-024)

implementation_statement: The BIA (P05), POL-01 section 11, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan (adopted 2026-09-11). Gap: customer-held program copies, the referral arrangement with another technician, and the sealed emergency access sheet are not in place yet (due 2026-12-31).
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-002, G-015)

implementation_statement: The library on the laptop syncs to the business file plan, which keeps prior versions for 30 days (provider). Owner responsibility: there is no backup independent of sync, ransomware on the laptop would sync encrypted files, and a restore has never been tried. Plan: weekly encrypted backup to two rotating external drives kept offline (one off site), customer-held copies after each visit, and a test restore every quarter (first by 2026-10-31).
evidence: File plan settings; P07 test restore 2026-08-26
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-023, G-034)

provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite provider; accounting SaaS provider
implementation_statement: Every service uses a named account for one person. The owner shares no logins; the bookkeeper and the IT consultant use their own accounts or sessions. (Shared operator logins on some customer HMIs are the customers' own systems, outside this boundary.)
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-016)

provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite provider; accounting SaaS provider; router maker (cloud portal)
implementation_statement: The productivity suite administrator account requires an authenticator app code. Gap: the accounting SaaS owner account (administrator) and the router cloud portal account sign in with a password only, although both offer MFA. The owner turns MFA on for both by 2026-09-30.
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-017)

implementation_statement: SaaS passwords are unique and saved in the browser. Gap: about 140 customer machine passwords (PLC, HMI, drive, and plant Wi-Fi) are in an unprotected spreadsheet in cloud storage, and the router's local admin password was the factory default until 2026-08-27. Plan: a password manager with a separate vault per customer; delete the spreadsheet; ask each customer to change shared machine passwords when the owner's work for it ends.
evidence: Cloud storage review 2026-08-25; P07 router test 2026-08-27
regulatory_driver: Customer A exhibit S1 (P03 G-036); Customer B and C NDAs (P03 G-044); CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-016)

implementation_statement: The P08 notification matrix (adopted 2026-09-11) lists every notice with its deadline: Customer A within 24 hours (exhibit S4), Customers B and C promptly (NDAs), and voluntary reports to the FBI and CISA. Gap: contacts not yet printed and the 24-hour notice never rehearsed (due 2026-10-31).
regulatory_driver: Customer A exhibit S4 (CIP-013-2 R1.2.1 flow-down; P03 G-039); Customer B and C NDAs (P03 G-045); CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-033)

implementation_statement: The ransomware runbook (P08) was adopted on 2026-09-11 with a contact list. Gap: not yet walked through with the IT consultant (due 2026-10-31).
regulatory_driver: Customer A exhibit S4 (P03 G-039); CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-015, G-031, G-032)

implementation_statement: The IT consultant's remote-support sessions on the laptop are started and watched by the owner; unattended access is off; the consultant signed the owner's NDA on 2026-08-20. Sessions are noted in the security log.
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-029)

implementation_statement: Gap: the old laptop (replaced in 2025) still holds a copy of the library, and USB sticks are reused across customers without wiping. By 2026-10-31 the owner has the old laptop drive wiped or destroyed with a record, and wipes each USB stick before it is used for another customer.
regulatory_driver: Customer A exhibit S7 (P03 G-042); CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-010)

implementation_statement: USB sticks are used only for machines that cannot load programs over a cable. Gap: the 8 sticks are not encrypted, are not scanned before they are plugged into a machine, and are used for more than one customer. Plan: one labeled, encrypted stick per customer, scanned on the laptop before each use, and the Customer A scanning station every time.
regulatory_driver: Customer A exhibit S3 (P03 G-038); CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-030)

implementation_statement: First risk assessment completed 2026-08-28 using NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Reviewed each August and after a new customer contract, a new system, or an incident.
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-013)

implementation_statement: Business-grade plans are used for email, files, and accounting. The productivity suite provider's SOC 2 Type 2 report was reviewed on 2026-08-26 (P09). Gap: the vibration analytics trial was started on click-through terms that let the vendor use uploaded data to improve its service, and Customer A's written consent was not obtained (exhibit S1); no list of external services and what customer data each holds.
regulatory_driver: Customer A exhibit S1 (P03 G-036); CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-005, G-006)

implementation_statement: The laptop's host firewall is on. On customer sites the laptop is cabled only to the machine network the job needs. Gap: the home network is shared with household devices; the legacy engineering virtual machine is bridged to whatever network the laptop is on; Wi-Fi stays on while the laptop is cabled to a machine network. Plan: separate business Wi-Fi at home (household devices on the guest network), virtual machine set to host-only except when cabled to a machine, Wi-Fi off when cabled to a machine (by 2026-10-31).
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-024, G-027)

provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite provider; accounting SaaS provider
implementation_statement: The laptop uses built-in full-disk encryption and the phone is encrypted. The SaaS providers encrypt stored data (inherited; SOC 2 report for the productivity suite). Gap: USB sticks are not encrypted, and the password spreadsheet is an ordinary file.
regulatory_driver: Customer A exhibit S1 (P03 G-036); Customer B and C NDAs (P03 G-044); CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-021)

implementation_statement: Automatic OS updates are on for the laptop and phone, and the SaaS providers patch their services. Gap: engineering software is updated only when a job needs it, and the legacy virtual machine runs an operating system that no longer gets updates. Plan: check the automation makers' update and advisory pages monthly; isolate the virtual machine (SC-7) until the legacy package can be retired.
evidence: Update history; virtual machine OS version
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-011, G-025)

implementation_statement: The laptop's built-in antivirus runs real-time and scheduled scans with automatic updates (P07 test 2026-08-26). Gap: the legacy virtual machine has no malicious code protection.
evidence: Antivirus status page; P07 test file
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-030)

implementation_statement: No integrity check was made before this assessment. From 2026-09-11 (POL-01 7.4) the owner checks the hash value Customer A provides before loading any firmware or software onto Customer A or utility equipment and records the check on the job ticket. By 2026-12-31 the library index holds a hash for every program, so the version on a machine can be compared with the library copy.
evidence: Firmware load records for 4 substation cabinets in 2026 (no hash checks)
regulatory_driver: Customer A exhibit S5 (CIP-013-2 R1.2.5 flow-down; P03 G-040); CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-014, G-035)
